title: AWAKE  i works randomly,...when it decides

judgment.rationale: The Awake report is still too ambiguous about the selected mode and the exact wake/sleep transition to choose a safe code path, even though it clearly claims that Awake is interfering with normal sleep behavior.
evidence: The body says the user selected “Continue using the selected power saving combination” but then describes the system sleeping and later waking unexpectedly.
No version details beyond 0.100.2, no bug report ZIP, and no timed repro sequence are attached.
No maintainer reply or linked fix is present.
judgment.recommended_action: Ask for the exact Awake mode state, a step-by-step sleep/wake repro, and a fresh /bugreport capture before assuming which Awake state transition is wrong.

fix_assessment.rationale: The current report does not yet separate an Awake state-management bug from an external wake timer or a misunderstanding of which Awake mode was active.

issue_context.summary: The reporter says Awake is interfering with normal sleep behavior, but the issue text is still ambiguous about whether Awake was in passive mode, another keep-awake mode, or reacting to a later power event when the machine woke unexpectedly.
known_information: The issue is filed against PowerToys 0.100.2 and identifies the module as Awake.
The specific option named in the report is “Continue using the selected power saving combination”.
The expected result is suspension according to the system power plan after 5 or 15 minutes, while the actual result is described as a random later wake.
inferences: The report may involve Awake reapplying a state after a power event, but it could also reflect an external wake source unrelated to Awake.
Without an exact timeline, triage cannot tell whether the bug is “Awake prevented sleep” or “something woke the system after it slept normally.”
issue_context.analysis: The issue is real enough to keep in bug triage, but a fix plan would be premature because the triggering transition is still not pinned down. The next useful evidence is a single clean repro with the visible Awake mode state and a bundled diagnostic capture.
initial_investigation: Current Awake code distinguishes passive, indefinite, timed, and expirable modes and logs power-event reapplication paths in src/modules/Awake/Awake/Core/Manager.cs and Awake.ModuleServices/AwakeService.cs.
The issue body does not yet say which concrete mode the app still showed after the unexpected wake or whether other wake timers were active.

information_gaps.information: A short timed repro that lists the chosen Awake mode, the Windows sleep timeout, and what the machine does from idle to sleep to wake.
information_gaps.why_needed: That distinguishes “Awake prevented sleep” from “the machine slept and was later reawakened by another event.”
information_gaps.how_to_collect: From a fresh PowerToys launch, list the exact mode selected in Awake, the sleep timeout in Windows, and the observed sleep/wake timeline.

information_gaps.information: Whether Awake still shows passive mode or another keep-awake mode after the unexpected wake occurs.
information_gaps.why_needed: The visible mode state identifies whether Awake itself thinks it should still be holding the system awake.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: After the unexpected wake, open Awake and report the exact mode that is shown in the UI or tray menu.

information_gaps.information: A fresh PowerToys diagnostic ZIP captured immediately after reproducing the unexpected wake behavior.
information_gaps.why_needed: The packaged logs are needed to inspect Awake state transitions and any power-event handling around the repro.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Reproduce the problem and then post a new comment with /bugreport immediately afterward.

actions.label: Request Awake mode and wake evidence

comment.body:
Thanks for naming the exact Awake option you used. To separate an Awake state bug from a separate wake source, please provide:

1. Short numbered steps from a fresh PowerToys launch that include the selected Awake mode and your Windows sleep timeout.
2. Whether Awake still shows passive mode or another keep-awake mode after the unexpected wake happens.
3. A fresh diagnostic ZIP by reproducing the behavior and then posting a comment with /bugreport immediately afterward.

That will show whether Awake prevented sleep, reactivated itself later, or whether something else woke the machine after it had already suspended normally.
